rec.name: Cart Store Benefits (Icon + Text USP Strip with Optional Slider)
rec.status: Built — launched (tested by 3 reviewers, KVA approved)

what.text: A configurable Store Benefits section for the cart (cart page or mini-cart) that shows up to 4 USPs, each with an icon or logo image/SVG and text (for example free shipping from €35, 100-day returns, free spare-parts service, pay on invoice in 30 days with Klarna). It has two display styles. 'Normal' shows a static grid of benefits. 'Slider' shows a row of tappable icons, and tapping one reveals that benefit's headline and longer description underneath. The active icon can be swapped for a second 'active' icon or SVG. Text can be omitted entirely, so the section also works as a logo strip such as payment or brand logos. Benefits can be placed under the checkout button and made sticky or scrolling together with it.

why.text: The cart is the last point of doubt before checkout. Showing risk reducers (free shipping threshold, long return window, pay-later option) right next to the checkout button tackles the typical objections of shipping cost, fear of being stuck with the purchase and payment friction at the moment of decision. Icons make the USPs quick to scan. The slider lets you add more detail without pushing the checkout button down the page.

how.text: Built as a theme-settings-driven snippet 'store-benefits' (Liquid, CSS and a small JS click handler) plus a render call placed where the block should appear (cart template or mini-cart). Settings are exposed in Theme settings > Store Benefits. 'Normal' style renders a CSS grid of benefit items (icon + text). 'Slider' style renders a header row of icons with an underlined active state, and a content area that shows the headline and description of the active benefit. A click handler toggles the 'active' class. Per-benefit icon can be an uploaded image or pasted SVG (SVG overrides the image), with an optional separate active icon. The code is delivered as install instructions: step 1 creates the snippet, step 2 adds the render call. The ticket notes that the instructions must be made theme-independent (not every theme has main-product.liquid) and clear for non-experts. For sticky or scrolling behaviour, the benefits sit under the checkout button and scroll with it. This is handled via the separate 'CRO | Cart | Sticky and Scrolling Settings' element.

items: Background of the block (color, can be transparent)
Number of benefits in a row (desktop, max 4)
Number of benefits in a row (mobile)
Enable bold text (applies to all benefits)
Per benefit (up to 4): enable benefit, icon image, SVG (overrides image), active icon image, active SVG, text/headline, optional sub-text for slider
Per-benefit title in the editor for a better overview (requested by the reviewer)

dependencies.text: Shopify theme with access to code edits (snippets plus the cart template or mini-cart section). Theme settings schema entries (settings_schema.json) for all store-benefit settings, e.g. enable_store_benefits, store_benefits_style, benefit_svg_N, benefit_png_N, benefit_texte_N. The code uses the legacy img_url filter and lazyload classes, so the theme must support lazysizes or it falls back to plain images. The mini-cart section id 'shopify-section-mini-cart' is targeted for spacing. No metafields or apps are required. The slider script uses global const names, so only one slider instance per page is safe.

images.caption: Normal style, vertical layout: four benefits stacked with icon plus text (free shipping from €35, 100-day returns, free spare-parts service, Klarna invoice in 30 days)
Benefits in the cart area under the add-to-cart/checkout button, shown as compact two-column tiles (365-day warranty, return until Christmas) with payment logos above
Theme settings panel: enable toggle, Normal/Slider style, background colors, text color, padding, radius, gaps and benefits-per-row
Slider style rendered as a row of round image icons with a progress bar, and the settings for bold text, benefits per row (desktop/mobile), icon image, SVG and active icon
Per-benefit settings (enable benefit, icon image, SVG override, active icon, active SVG) with a reviewer request for a title field per benefit
